taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Cloud Run invoker identity, audience and application resource authority
controls.source_trace: Resolve which layer authenticates invokers and which maps them to application tenants/resources. Keep public service admission separate from sensitive handler authorization.
controls.implementation_branch: Distinguish service invoker IAM admission from application-level account/object checks. Verify the identity token audience expected by the configured service/custom audience and the actual ingress path. A publicly invokable service may be deliberate; the decisive issue is an unintended principal reaching protected application behavior, not the absence of an authentication prompt.
controls.operational_method: Record whether the invoker IAM check is disabled or whether allUsers has an invoker grant; these are different publication configurations. Identify which Authorization or X-Serverless-Authorization header the platform validates and what identity the application then verifies. In a supplied trace, separate platform admission from handler resource access. A public service intentionally returning public content remains the control; do not infer application authentication solely from the platform header being present.
controls.controlled_verification: Use an owned service fixture and synthetic response; compare intended invoker/audience with another owned principal or audience.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: A public URL or a platform 403 alone does not prove handler exposure or correct object authorization.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Align service admission and handler identity/resource checks, preserving expected service-to-service invocation.
